title: Family Dollar Stores Recalls Oscillating Ceramic Heater for Fire Hazard
summary: The heaters can overheat and smoke, which could pose a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 35,000 (17,000 with consumers).

title: Samara Brothers Recalls Children's Two-Piece Overall Sets, Snaps Contain Lead
summary: The coatings on the snaps in the overalls and shirt contain excessive amounts of lead, posing a serious risk of lead poisoning and adverse health effects to young children. Units: About 200.

title: DEWALT Recalls Portable Generators Due to Electric Shock Hazard
summary: A ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) installed on the generator could fail to operate properly, posing a risk of electric shock to consumers. Units: About 13,800.

title: Pentair Water Pool and Spa Inc. Recalls Gas Pool Heaters for Carbon Monoxide Hazard
summary: These pool heaters can emit excessive carbon monoxide (CO), posing a risk of CO poisoning in the event of a vent leak in an indoor installation. Units: About 105,000.

title: Nitrous Oxide Systems Recalls Snowmobile and ATV NOS Kit Bottles that Can Forcefully Burst
summary: An incorrect burst disc, a component of the NOS bottle valve, may have been installed in the recalled NOS Kits. If the bottle is overfilled and overheated, it could forcefully burst, posing an impact injury hazard to consumers. Units: About 16.

title: Geometix International LLC Recalls MagneBlocks™ Toys, Ingested Magnets Pose Aspiration and Intestinal Hazards
summary: Tiny magnets inside the building pieces can fall out. Magnets found by young children can be swallowed or aspirated. If more than one magnet is swallowed, the magnets can attract each other and cause intestinal perforation or blockage, which can be fatal. Units: About 40,000 sets.

title: Graco Children's Products Inc. Recalls to Repair Contempo™ Highchairs Due to Collapse Hazard
summary: The highchair can collapse if it is not fully opened and locked into place from the storage position prior to use. If the highchair collapses, a child occupying the highchair can be injured. Units: About 100,000.

title: Target Recalls Baby Rattles and Ornaments for Choking Hazard
summary: Small parts on the plush rattles and frame ornaments can break or detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. Additionally, the rattles' plastic ring can break and expose sharp points. Units: About 460,000.

title: U.S. Toy Co. Recalls More Children's Butterfly Necklaces Due to Lead Poisoning
summary: The pendant on the necklace contains high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects. Units: About 113,800 (This recall was first announced in Dec. 2006).

title: Kids II Inc. Recalls Teethers Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The flexible plastic ring that holds the teether beads in place can crack or break, and the beads can detach, posing a choking hazard to infants. Units: About 375,000.

title: Pumpkin Candle Holders Sold by QVC Recalled Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The product can crack, break or shatter when used with the tea light candles that accompany them, yielding sharp pieces of glass that pose a laceration hazard. Units: About 25,500.

title: Sportsstuff Inc. Recalls Air Pumps for Laceration Hazard
summary: These air pumps can overheat and explode during use, posing a risk of lacerations to the user and nearby consumers. Units: About 11,000.

title: Children's Hooded Sweatshirts with Drawstrings Recalled by Seena International for Strangulation Hazard
summary: The garments have a drawstring through the hood, posing a strangulation hazard to children. Units: About 45,000.

title: Kawasaki Motors Corp., U.S.A. Recalls 2007 KFX50 and KFX90 All-Terrain Vehicles
summary: On some of these units, the handlebar holder, tie-rod adjustment, and tie-rod end nuts may not have been tightened to the proper torque. Operation of the vehicle can cause the nuts to loosen, resulting in a loss of steering control. This poses a crash hazard, which can result in injury or death. Uni

title: Cannondale Recalls 2007 Model Road Bicycles Due to Brake Failure
summary: The bicycle's front brake can fail, causing the rider to lose control and fall. Units: About 700.

title: American Honda Motor Corp. Recalls All-Terrain Vehicles for Crash Hazard
summary: The front suspension arm ball joints could have been contaminated during production, resulting in rapid wear of one or more of the ball joints and possible ball joint separation. If the ball joint separation occurs while riding, the operator could lose control of the ATV. Units: About 11,000.

title: Gamewell-FCI Recalls to Upgrade Software Used with Fire Alarm System Control Boards
summary: Incoming and outgoing messages to and from the control board can interfere with each other, preventing it from sending a message to the command center in the event of fire. Units: About 700.

title: Hong Teng Trading (USA) Inc. Recalls Electric Oil Lamps Due To Shock and Fire Hazards
summary: The power cord is not polarized and is undersized. The power cord is not correctly secured and there is no strain relief on the switch housing. Additionally, the switch housing is not flame-retardant. As a result of these issues, the lamps pose shock and fire hazards. Units: About 3,900.

title: Old Williamsburgh Candle Corp. Recalls Mason Jar Candles Due To Laceration and Burn Hazard
summary: The wick can move from the center of the jar to the side, causing the glass to overheat and possibly crack or shatter. Exposure to broken glass and molten wax poses laceration and burn hazards to consumers. Units: About 3.7 million.

title: Flojet Recalls VAC Pumps Sold With LeBleu 50-Gallon Bottled Water System for Shock Hazard
summary: A manufacturing defect can cause consumers to receive an electric shock when the metal housing is touched. Units: About 500.

title: Home Decorators Collection Recalls Storage Trunks Due to Entrapment and Suffocation Hazards
summary: The trunk has an exterior clasp that can lock unexpectedly when the trunk lid closes. If a child climbs inside the trunk, he/she may not be able to open the trunk from the inside. This poses an entrapment and suffocation hazard to children. Units: About 500.

title: Sally Foster Inc. Recalls Tea Lights Candles for Fire Hazard
summary: The tea light candles have a clear, plastic shell that can melt or ignite, posing a fire or burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 46,800 sets.

title: TAC LLC Recalls "Erie Boiler Boss" Boiler Controls for Scald Hazard
summary: These boiler controls can fail, causing water temperature to rise to the high temperature limit. Should the high temperature thermostat or external safety limit devices also fail, consumers could suffer scalds from unexpectedly hot water during use or system piping damage can result. Units: About 85

title: Hair Dryers Recalled by Version-X Due to Electrocution Hazard
summary: These electric hair dryers are not equipped with an immersion protection plug to prevent electrocution if the hair dryer falls into water. title: Tower Fans Recalled by the Holmes Group Due to Fire Hazard
summary: Electrical arcing in the fan's wiring can cause a fire hazard. Units: About 300,000.

title: Arctic Cat Recalls Model Year 2007 90cc Youth Model ATVs
summary: On the recalled ATVs, the handlebar base mounting bolts, tie-rod ends and tie-rod adjustment locking nuts may not have been tightened to the proper torque during the production process. Operating an affected ATV could cause components to loosen, resulting in loss of steering control. This condition

title: DS Waters of America Inc. Recalls Water Coolers for Fire Hazard
summary: A water leak inside the water cooler can create an electrical arc, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 8,700.

title: Next Step Plastic Sippy/Tumbler Cups Recalled for Laceration Hazard
summary: The impact of being dropped or banged can cause the cup to break into pieces, resulting in sharp or jagged edges that pose a laceration hazard to children. Units: About 43,500.

title: Weil-McLain Co. Recalls Boilers for Leaking Exhaust, Carbon Monoxide
summary: The boiler assembly is not properly sealed. Exhaust and carbon monoxide (CO) can leak during operation and accumulate, posing a risk of poisoning. Units: 171.
